📖 The tool

From a rough idea to an essay that holds together.

Use the feedback your draft needs, when you need it. Explore an idea, untangle a paragraph, sharpen a point of view, or check a recommendation. There is no syllabus to finish.

Clarity

📝 Find the point

Choose your reader. Name the question. Separate your claim from the observations supporting it.

You make: a thesis and argument map.
Reasoning

🔎 Earn the conclusion

Find hidden assumptions, consider a strong objection, and revise without making your evidence sound stronger than it is.

You make: a first complete essay.
Structure

🧭 Give it shape

Compare alternatives when relevant. Order your paragraphs around the reader’s questions. Replace vague language with precise meaning.

You make: a structured second draft.
Voice

✍️ Make it yours

Edit with intention. Keep the details, rhythm, and perspective that make this piece yours.

You keep: the final say on every revision.

🧠 See the revision, not just the polish.

Know what changed.
Know what you can do next.

Keep your original beside each revision. See which passages need attention and why. Accept useful suggestions and leave the rest.

We’re designing feedback around clear criteria, not a mysterious “good writing” score. AI assessments are guidance, and may be wrong. You decide what to keep.

📚 A process with a foundation.

Established ideas. Thoughtful feedback.

Our five-phase engine draws on established approaches to argument, uncertainty, decision-making, and structure. Apply them where they fit your essay; their combination is our design, not a scientifically validated scoring system.

  1. Map the argument: claim, evidence, and the bridge between them, inspired by Stephen Toulmin’s The Uses of Argument.
  2. Stress-test the idea: consider objections and possible failure, informed by Gary Klein’s Premortem Method.
  3. Question assumptions: distinguish confidence from support, informed by Kahneman and Tversky’s work on judgment under uncertainty.
  4. Frame the choice: compare alternatives when making a recommendation, informed by the reversible-decision distinction.
  5. Shape the draft: organize supporting ideas around a main point, inspired by Barbara Minto’s Pyramid Principle.

The core review workflow, prompts, and provider interface are open source. The paid tool will provide hosted AI feedback, saved drafts, revision history, and a simple writing experience.

You can inspect the engine today. The hosted writing tool is in development.

Explore the open-source engine
Will AI write my essay?

The tool is designed to help you practice. AI points out weaknesses and guides revision; you write the work and decide which suggestions to accept.

Do I need an AI subscription?

The planned hosted tool includes a stated feedback allowance. You won’t need to provide your own AI key or subscription.

Does this guarantee improvement?

No. Independent exercises are designed to help you observe progress. We have not yet validated improvement outcomes for this tool.

Can I use the full tool today?

Not yet. Explore the sample now. Paid access will open once delivery, billing, and support are ready.
